title: Project reference note: retrieval and fine-tuning
source: Locally authored teaching note; not an external authority
text: Retrieval-augmented generation supplies selected external passages to a language model at inference time. Updating the indexed documents can change available evidence without retraining the model. Fine-tuning updates model parameters using training examples. It can adapt style or behavior, but frequent factual changes generally require updating training data and another training process if stored only in model weights. Retrieval still depends on source quality, indexing, and retrieval relevance; it does not guarantee correctness.

title: Project reference note: supervised and unsupervised learning
source: Locally authored teaching note; not an external authority
text: Supervised learning uses input examples paired with target labels, such as emails labelled spam or not spam. Unsupervised learning seeks structure without supplied target labels, such as clustering similar customer profiles. Evaluation differs by task: a labelled held-out set can measure classification accuracy, while clustering requires appropriate structure or downstream usefulness criteria.

title: Synthetic benchmark: fictional Aurora battery experiment
source: Synthetic controlled evidence for testing only
text: In the fictional Aurora experiment, battery A lasted 8 hours and cost 40 credits. Battery B lasted 10 hours and cost 60 credits. Both were tested at the same temperature on the same workload. Only one trial was run for each battery. No production reliability data was collected. These figures are synthetic, not real product measurements.
